lines.trans: What did you overhear last night?
Nothing at all.
You did hear it—you heard something big enough to make you answer "nothing at all"!
Whatever you heard or whatever you saw yesterday, none of it is true.
Telling lies is my drinking habit—my nickname is the Drunken Liar!

words.gloss: is my drinking habit, you see

lines.trans: So what exactly did you hear?
I think I overheard a bit of the lies you told yesterday.
Calling him a cruel jerk, asking why he went on a matchmaking date, and asking "so what if the prosecutor is pretty"!
And "if you were going to do that, why did you kiss me"!
Stop, that is enough—it was all a lie anyway!

examples.text: 야, 오만 원은 까야지. 어젯밤에 우리 집에서 잤잖아.
examples.trans: Hey, I have to deduct fifty thousand won. You slept at our place last night.
The topic of last night came up during this shoot.

meanings.note: colloquial contraction of 무엇; also used rhetorically to brush off a question

examples.trans: What are you doing now?
Why are you even asking something like that?

meanings.note: verb listen

examples.trans: Listen well.
Listen to a song.

examples.text: 뭘 어떻게 해야 할지 모르겠으면 아무것도 안 하면 돼요.
examples.trans: If you don't know what to do, you don't have to do anything at all.
The topic of anything at all came up during this shoot.

meanings.en: to do, to perform, to hold
meanings.note: Core verb; also combines with nouns to form verbs.

examples.trans: What are you doing right now?
We are holding a meeting today.
The atmosphere today is really worth, likely to.
That person always looks worth, likely to.

meanings.note: refers to something known to both speakers or near the listener

examples.trans: That movie was really fun.
What is that person's name?

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (pron).

examples.text: 들었네, 아무것도라고 할 만한 그 무언가를 들었어!
examples.trans: You did hear it—you heard something big enough to make you answer "nothing at all"!
Here the word for 'something' is key.
Do you have time today?
Where are you going?

meanings.note: Used only with close friends, younger people, or children

examples.trans: Did you hear about this yesterday?
I was busy today because of yesterday.

meanings.note: Interrogative or indefinite pronoun; often shortened to 뭐 in casual speech.

examples.trans: What is your favorite food?
What can I help you with?

보다.gloss: to see, to watch; to take (an exam)

meanings.en: to see, to look at, to watch
meanings.note: Primary meaning.
Idiomatic in 시험을 보다.

examples.trans: I watched a movie on the weekend.
I took the driver's license exam.

meanings.note: Demonstrative pronoun referring to something near the listener or already mentioned. Routinely spoken as 그거. RR: geugeot; spoken geugeo.

examples.trans: That is my mobile phone.
That is really important.

meanings.en: actually, in fact, to tell the truth
meanings.note: adverbial use of the noun 사실 (fact)

examples.trans: Honestly, I don't know well either.
In fact, I couldn't sleep yesterday.

meanings.note: Negative copula used with nouns (often with -이/가)

examples.trans: It is not my fault.
Today is not Sunday, it's Monday.

examples.text: 그래, 예진이 너 왜 나한테 거짓말했어?
examples.trans: Yeah, Ye-jin, why did you lie to me?

examples.text: 이번 일은 꼭 잘 해결해 봐요, 거짓말하다는 마음으로요.
examples.trans: Let's make sure we handle this well (lied).

meanings.note: Bound noun often contracted to 거 in everyday speech.

examples.trans: This is my bag.
Because I think I'm late.

meanings.note: Plain first-person singular pronoun used with friends, younger people, or subordinates; contracts to 난 with -는 and becomes 내가 before -가.

examples.trans: I'm going to stay home today.
I'll go first.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 설령 조금 취했다 해도 술버릇이 굉장히 깔끔한 편이라.
examples.trans: Even supposing I do get slightly tipsy, my drinking habits are remarkably neat.
Here the word for 'drinking habit' is key.

examples.text: 사람들이 연예인 이름 앞에 별명을 붙였는데 웃기더라고.
examples.trans: People put nicknames in front of celebrities' names, and it was really funny.

examples.text: 나도 그런 식의 별명이 생겼으면 좋겠다는 거지.
examples.trans: So I hope I get a nickname like that too.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 거짓말하는 게 내 술버릇이거든, 내 별명이 취중구라야!
examples.trans: Telling lies is my drinking habit—my nickname is the Drunken Liar!
Here the word for 'is Drunken Fibber!' is key.

meanings.note: adverb therefore

examples.trans: So how is it?
So I went.
Please give me some water.
Please wait just a moment.

meanings.note: Contraction of 조금
Used in -(으)ㄴ/는 것 같다 to express 'it seems that...' or 'I think...'.

meanings.en: to be the same, to be like
meanings.note: Compares two things with -와/과 같다.

examples.trans: I think I'm late.
It looks like it's going to rain.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (adj).

examples.text: 얘 지금 살려고 발버둥 치는 거 안 보여? 이런 거 보면 인간이 진짜 제일 잔인해.
examples.trans: Do you not see it struggling to stay alive right now? Seeing things like this, humans really are the cruelest.
This expression comes from 'are cruel'.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.trans: That is why you are a cruel jerk, do you know that?
Here the word for 'guy, jerk' is key.

meanings.note: Interrogative adverb.

examples.trans: Why are you running?
Why were you late today?

meanings.note: Used in 선을 긋다 (to draw the line / set boundaries)

examples.trans: Please do not step outside the line.
I drew a line between work and private life.

examples.text: 선? 검사? 설마 검사가 예쁘기까지 하겠어?
examples.trans: A blind date? A prosecutor? Could a prosecutor really be pretty too?
The topic of prosecutor came up during this shoot.

meanings.note: Spoken variant of 예쁘다.

examples.trans: The flowers are really pretty.
pretty clothes

meanings.note: Placed before the verb it modifies.

examples.trans: I finished all my homework.
I ate all the rice.

그러다.gloss: to say so; to do so

meanings.en: to say so; to speak like that
meanings.note: contracted from 그러하다; often follows quoted speech

meanings.en: to do so; to act like that

examples.trans: Who said that?
That friend also said they are going together.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 그럴 거면 나한테 뽀뽀는 왜 했는데?
examples.trans: If you were going to do that, why did you kiss me?
Here the word for 'a kiss' is key.

meanings.note: Often used as a command or suggestion to stop.

examples.trans: Please stop now.
Let's stop fighting.

meanings.note: Takes a complement marked with 이/가.

examples.trans: I want to become a doctor.
It has already become 12 o'clock.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (adv).

examples.trans: Stop, that is enough—it was all a lie anyway!
Here the word for 'anyway, in any case' is key.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 아니, 핑크가 어려운 게 아니라 그런 거짓말이 어렵다고요.
examples.trans: No, it is not that pink is difficult—telling that kind of lie is difficult.
Here the word for 'lie' is key.

meanings.note: Used in standard farewells 안녕히 계세요 and 안녕히 가세요.

examples.trans: Goodbye! (to someone staying)
Goodbye! (to someone leaving)

meanings.note: Honorific equivalent of 있다; used in 안녕히 계세요 ('goodbye' to someone staying).

examples.trans: Goodbye! (to someone staying)
Is the teacher inside right now?
